dossier.public_summary: The dips at 13.3 days are not steady: odd and even dips differ significantly and depths vary between transits and between pipeline products. That pattern matches a stellar binary (possibly blended) more than a planet. No on-target centroid is available and the signal resembles several known false positives.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ by 3.957 sigma with 5398 ppm (~2.2x) deeper evens; seen in one of the three sectors with consistent sign, as expected for an eclipsing binary at twice the 13.3 d period (26.6 d) rather than a planet at 13.3 d.

Individual transits are not consistent with one depth; one transit around BTJD 3016.837 is far shallower than the others, and the top three carry 91.6% of the signal. Combined with sector-depth change, this favours spot crossings/systematics or blending over a steady planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes significantly between sectors. sector_depths_by_source shows verdict differs_by_source: QLP sectors 90,91 depth_ppm 14588 err 1495 p_constant 0.9862544601599441 vs TESS-SPOC sector 63 depth_ppm 6706 err 1234 p_constant 1.0. Calibration difference explains the average shift, but the per-transit scatter above remains inconsistent for a planet.
Independent planet scorer rates this in the lowest decile, consistent with the binary-like odd/even and transit-to-transit variation.
